# McSween Transport: database map

<!-- Generated by `node tools/data-model.mjs`. Don't edit by hand: change the entity
     files or entityAccess, then run it again. A test fails while this file is out of date. -->

Every kind of record the app keeps, its fields, how records point at each other,
and who can see them. Built from `base44/entities/*.jsonc`,
`supabase/entity-tables.json` and `base44/functions/entityAccess/entry.ts`.

## How the data is kept

- Each kind of record (an **entity**, like `Trip`) is a table. Base44 holds the live data today;
  the Supabase copy has one table per entity in the `public` schema, with the same field names
  (table names are snake_case: `Trip` is `trip`, `User` is `app_user`).
- Ids are text (Base44's 24-character ids), not numbers. A field ending in `_id` usually holds
  another record's id; the **Links** lines below say which.
- Every record also has these fields, left out of the tables below:
  `id` (text): The record's id: 24 characters, text (not a number).
  `created_date` (timestamptz): When the record was made.
  `updated_date` (timestamptz): When it last changed.
  `created_by` (text): Email of whoever made it, when made from the app.
  `created_by_id` (text): User id of whoever made it.
  `is_sample` (boolean): Base44 sample data.
- Names are often copied next to ids (`vehicle_name` beside `vehicle_id`) so lists show without
  extra reads. The id is the truth; the copied name can be out of date.
- No foreign keys yet: older Base44 data can point at records that were deleted.
- **The browser never reads a table.** The app asks the server function `entityAccess`
  (browser side: `src/lib/scopedEntities.js`) or a purpose-built function (`driverPhone`,
  `kioskCheckIn`, `accessRoles`, ...). On Supabase every table has row level security on and
  no policies, so only the server can touch the data.
- Secrets are never sent to the browser: entityAccess removes these fields from every answer,
  wherever they appear: `driver_pin`, `entry_code`, `access_code`, `one_time_code`, `one_time_code_expires_at`, `nfc_tag_id`, `nfc_card_tag`, `nfc_card_uid`, `card_uid`, `card_tag`, `pairing_code`, `token`, `token_hash`, `salt`, `pin_hash`, `password`, `device_token`, `driver_grant`, `verification_grant`.
- Passengers never see other passengers' pickup locations: a passenger's own `User` record is
  the only one they can read, and the `Trip` fields they get leave out passenger names, phones and
  exact pickup and drop-off locations.

## Who can see what

Roles (`User.role`): **admin**, **company** (a company's manager), **mechanic**, and phone users
(**staff**, **passenger**, **driver**). Drivers on a bus tablet have no sign-in: the tablet's own
functions act for them. A person can also have a custom role (`User.access_role_id`, see
`AccessRole` and `RoleAssignment`); they work through the role workspace (`accessRoles` function),
and through entityAccess can only read their own profile.

"Own company" means a company the person is an approved member of (`CompanyMembership`). A record
belongs to a company through its bus (`vehicle_id`), else its driver (`driver_id`), else its
`company_id`. Mechanics are not tied to one company.

Changing records through entityAccess:

- **admin**: any record (except invoices, made only in billing, and app errors, which can only be marked fixed).
- **company**: records of the kinds it can read, for its own company; it can't make a new `Company`.
- **mechanic**: maintenance records (`Vehicle`, `Fault`, `Inspection`, `InspectionResult`, `InspectionTemplate`, `Part`, `MaintenanceSchedule`, `MaintenanceSettings`) and the mechanic chat;
  on `Vehicle` only odometer, hours, status and inspection fields. Deleting maintenance records is admin-only.
- **staff / passenger**: their own profile fields, their own staff-chat messages and lost-item reports.

### InspectionTemplate

Table `inspection_template` · belongs to a company through `company_id` · read and changed through entityAccess.

**Links to:** [Company](#company) (`company_id`).

**Linked from:** [Inspection](#inspection).template_id.

| Field | Type | Notes |

| `name` | text | e.g. Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Service. Required. |
| `category` | text |  |
| `company_id` | text | → Company. Optional — blank means available to every company (true for the default seeded templates). |
| `company_name` | text |  |
| `frequency_days` | double precision | Optional — how often (in days) this template should be run per vehicle. Set this to have inspectionAlerts remind mechanics when a vehicle is overdue. Leave blank/0 to exclude this template from reminders (e.g. a one-off or ad-hoc checklist). |
| `audience` | text | Who runs this inspection: mechanics (Run Inspection page), drivers (driver tablet app), or both. One of: `mechanic`, `driver`, `both`. Default `"mechanic"`. |
| `driver_trigger` | text | When the inspection appears in the driver app. One of: `start_of_day`, `at_times`, `shift_start`, `shift_end`, `on_demand`. Default `"start_of_day"`. |
| `driver_days` | jsonb (list) | Days of the week it appears (0=Sunday … 6=Saturday). Empty means every day. |
| `driver_times` | jsonb (list) | For the 'at_times' trigger: HH:MM times of day it becomes due (each time is a separate round, so it can be due several times a day). |
| `driver_vehicle_ids` | jsonb (list) | Only send to these buses. Empty means every bus (in the template's company). |
| `xray_layout` | text | Which bus drawing the X-ray walk-around uses. One of: `front_engine`, `minibus`, `city_rear`. Default `"front_engine"`. |
| `driver_from_time` | text | Optional HH:MM — only appears from this time of day on. |
| `driver_required` | boolean | Driver must finish it before driving (no skip). Default `true`. |
| `driver_sent_at` | timestamptz | Set by 'Send to drivers now' — the inspection pops up on every matching driver tablet until done after this time. |
| `sections` | jsonb (list) |  |

**Linked from:** [ClientError](#clienterror).device_id, [DeviceCredential](#devicecredential).device_id, [DriverShift](#drivershift).device_id, [PhoneUnlock](#phoneunlock).device_id, [PushToken](#pushtoken).device_id, [StaffCheckIn](#staffcheckin).device_id, [TabletRecordingSession](#tabletrecordingsession).device_id, [TabletSupportSession](#tabletsupportsession).device_id, [VerificationGrant](#verificationgrant).device_id.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `support_request` | jsonb | Not sent to the browser. Set by the server only. |

| `device_info` | text | Reported by the tablet: which map it can draw (full/basic), WebGL 2 support and browser. |

| `last_seen` | timestamptz |  |
| `paired` | boolean | Default `false`. Changed only through access-code management. |
| `pairing_code` | text | **Secret**: never sent to the browser. Changed only through access-code management. |

| `network_command` | jsonb | Admin → Kiosk tablets: a pending Wi-Fi or hotspot command for this tablet (a Wi-Fi change includes its password). Not returned by entityAccess; given only to the tablet on check-in and deleted once the tablet confirms it, or after 10 minutes. Not sent to the browser. |
| `network_status` | jsonb | Latest admin network command delivery and native completion status; no passwords. Set by the server only. |
| `control_command` | jsonb | Private admin command; native executor verifies over fixed HTTPS endpoint. Never exposed through entity gateway. Not sent to the browser. |
| `control_status` | jsonb | Safe command progress. Requested is not proof that reboot completed. Set by the server only. |
| `display_layout` | text | One of: `auto`, `tablet`, `phone`. Default `"auto"`. |
| `pickup_sign` | jsonb | Not sent to the browser. |
| `recordings_request` | jsonb | Not sent to the browser. Set by the server only. |
| `native_tracking_health` | jsonb | Server-timestamped native background GPS telemetry; never an authorization source. |

## Other storage (Supabase only)

Not app records; the server's own bookkeeping. None of it is reachable from the browser.

- `public.storage_file_copy`: which Base44 file was copied to which Supabase storage file (one copy per storage area).
- `tt_atomic.attempt_reservation`, `tt_atomic.budget_policy`, `tt_atomic.operation_receipt`: rate limits, and
  receipts so a retried save is only done once.
- `tablet_support.sessions`, `tablet_support.events`: remote-support sessions with the bus tablets and their audit trail.
- `tt_ops`: scheduled jobs (pg_cron). `prune_location_pings` keeps 90 days of `LocationPing`; `run_scheduled_function`
  starts the scheduled server functions.
- `private.link_app_user`: links a Supabase sign-in (`auth.users`) to its `app_user` once the email is confirmed.
- Storage areas (buckets): `public` (logos, bus and profile photos, ads: anyone with the link),
  `private` (check-in pictures, signatures, chat, incident and inspection photos, driver documents:
  short-lived signed links only), `downloads` (tablet app updates).
